title: Hantavirus Kills Three on Cruise Ship MV Hondius
excerpt: The Dutch-flagged vessel docks in Tenerife on May 11 as WHO coordinates a global evacuation of nearly 150 passengers across four continents.
body:
A deadly hantavirus outbreak aboard the Dutch-flagged cruise ship MV Hondius has triggered a multinational emergency response, with the vessel docking at Granadilla Port in Tenerife on Sunday after weeks stranded at sea.

**What happened aboard the MV Hondius:**
The outbreak of Andes virus infection was identified in April 2026 aboard the MV Hondius, which left Ushuaia, Argentina on 1 April 2026. As of 4 May, seven cases — two laboratory confirmed and five suspected — had been identified, including three deaths, with illness onset between 6 and 28 April characterized by fever, rapid progression to pneumonia, and acute respiratory distress. Authorities confirmed the Andes virus, normally found in South America, was responsible; unlike most hantaviruses, it can spread between people in rare cases, and some on-board spread has been at least partially attributed to human-to-human transmission.

**Why this outbreak is uniquely alarming:**
Health authorities on four continents were tracking down and monitoring more than two dozen passengers who left the ship before the outbreak was first detected on May 2, and scrambling to trace others who may have had contact with them. The MV Hondius has only a small, routine medical facility on board — stocked with anti-inflammatory drugs and oxygen tanks — lacking the scanners or ventilators needed to treat serious respiratory illness. WHO currently assesses the risk to the global population as low and will continue to monitor the epidemiological situation.

**The evacuation plan and what comes next:**
WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus traveled to Tenerife personally to oversee the evacuation, stressing that this is 'not another Covid-19' and that passengers would be ferried ashore in sealed, guarded vehicles before direct repatriation to their home countries. A CDC team has been dispatched to meet returning American passengers in Nebraska, where the 17 US passengers — none currently showing symptoms — will be monitored at the National Quarantine Unit at the University of Nebraska Medical Center. Watch whether any new cases emerge among the more than two dozen passengers already repatriated globally, and whether contact tracing closes the loop on everyone who disembarked before May 2.
